verifications.claim: Discussions regarding the 25th Amendment and Donald Trump resurfaced as of April 2026.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Donald Trump is suddenly facing increased 25th amendment calls... after Trump posted a threat for Iran... on Easter Sunday'; R5: 'Trump Triggers 25th Amendment Calls With Unhinged Easter Meltdown'; R7: 'Apr 09 Democrats grow bolder... after his Iran threats'; 'Apr 06 Could the 25th Amendment be invoked against Trump?'
verifications.reasoning: References describe recent (Easter ~April 2026) discussions triggered by Trump's posts, implying resurgence after prior instances, but no explicit 'April 2026' or 'resurfaced' phrasing.

verifications.claim: Section 4 of the 25th Amendment allows the Vice President and a majority of the Cabinet to remove a president deemed unable to discharge their duties.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Section 4... provides a mechanism for the Vice President and a majority of... the Cabinet... to declare that the president is unable to discharge the powers and duties'; R2: discusses VP and Cabinet vote to remove; R5: 'the vice president and a majority of the Cabinet could opt to replace the president due to an inability to discharge their duties'
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches standard description of Section 4 in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Reports indicate calls for removal followed Donald Trump's Easter social media posts containing threats against the Strait of Hormuz.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '25th amendment became a talking point only after Trump posted a threat... “...Open the F****n’ Strait, you crazy b******s...' on Easter Sunday'; R5: 'profane Easter morning Truth Social post... 'Open the F--kin’ Strait...' triggering 25th Amendment calls'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly link Easter Truth Social post threatening the Strait to 25th Amendment removal calls.

verifications.claim: Under Section 4 of the 25th Amendment, if the President contests their removal, the Vice President keeps power only if two-thirds of both the House and Senate agree.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'If the president contests it... A two-thirds vote in both the House and Senate is required to keep the Vice President as Acting President'; R2: 'unless... two-thirds majorities in both the House and Senate to block him [president resumes office]'
verifications.reasoning: Precise match to Section 4 process description.

verifications.claim: The 25th Amendment has never been used.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R5: 'The 25th Amendment was first used by Nixon in 1973... most recently used by Biden in 2021'; R6: 'never-used constitutional provision' (context Sec4); R7: 'Section 4... has never been used'
verifications.reasoning: R5 directly states the Amendment has been used (Sections 1-3), contradicting the absolute claim; others specify Section 4 never used, creating contradiction.

verifications.claim: The 25th Amendment was previously discussed regarding Donald Trump in 2021 following the Capitol riot.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'after the riot [Jan 6, 2021]... cabinet members were discussing invoking the 25th Amendment'; R7: 'Jan 12... after the deadly pro-Trump riot'; 'Jan 08... Capitol... by a pro-Trump mob'; 'Schumer... Pelosi... 25th Amendment' post-Capitol riot
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm 2021 Capitol riot discussions of 25th Amendment re: Trump.
